title: Information-Geometric Bound on the Robustness of Entanglement Generation
summary: Entanglement generation is a central resource for quantum information processing, quantum networking, and quantum sensing. In practical implementations, however, entangling interactions are inevitably subject to uncertainty and fluctuations in the interaction strength. We investigate the robustness of entanglement generation in the presence of such imperfections and establish a direct connection between the robustness of entanglement generation and quantum Fisher information (QFI). For two interacting qubits, we show that the reduction in concurrence caused by fluctuations in the interaction parameter is bounded by the QFI with respect to the interaction strength.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a direct connection between the robustness of entanglement generation and quantum Fisher information (QFI), showing that for two interacting qubits, the reduction in concurrence due to fluctuations in interaction strength is bounded by the QFI with respect to that interaction parameter.
AI.motivation: Entanglement generation is a key resource for quantum information processing, but in practice, entangling interactions suffer from uncertainty and fluctuations in interaction strength. The motivation is to investigate and quantify the robustness of entanglement generation under such imperfections.
AI.method: The authors establish a theoretical connection between entanglement robustness and quantum Fisher information (QFI). For two interacting qubits, they analyze how fluctuations in the interaction parameter affect concurrence and bound this reduction using QFI.
AI.result: For two interacting qubits, the reduction in concurrence caused by fluctuations in the interaction parameter is bounded by the QFI with respect to the interaction strength.
AI.conclusion: There is a direct quantitative link between entanglement robustness and quantum Fisher information, providing a fundamental bound that relates metrological sensitivity to entanglement resilience under parameter fluctuations.

title: Symmetries and overparametrization properties of Hamiltonian variational ansatzes for the $(1+1)$d $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory
summary: We perform detailed studies of five Hamiltonian variational ansatzes (HVA) based on the Hamiltonian of the $(1+1)$d $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory. The ansatzes are designed to respect local and global symmetries of the original Hamiltonian and therefore act on a finely segmented state Hilbert space. Following Larocca et al. (2023), we numerically study the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra (DLA) and the rank of the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) of the ansatzes within specific invariant subspaces. The ansatzes all involve sums of weight-three Paulis in their generators, which is a feature that have so far been underexplored in this context. We also perform numerical experiments to determine the ground state energy of the original Hamiltonian via variational quantum eigensolver (VQE), and observe that overparametrization of the ansatzes coincides with the apparent disappearance of local minima in the loss function, in line with the finding in the reference. Finally, the decay rate of the VQE loss function under gradient descent optimization is revealed to scale linearly with the number of parameters in the ansatz. These results help to enrich the theory of overparameterization of quantum circuits and inform the design of scalable variational ansatzes.

AI.tldr: The paper studies five Hamiltonian variational ansatzes (HVA) for the (1+1)d Z₂ lattice gauge theory, analyzing their dynamical Lie algebras, quantum Fisher information matrices, and overparameterization behavior in VQE for ground state energy estimation.
AI.motivation: To understand the properties of symmetry-preserving Hamiltonian variational ansatzes—particularly those using weight-three Pauli generators—and to investigate overparameterization phenomena in quantum circuits for lattice gauge theories.
AI.method: Numerical study of the dimension of dynamical Lie algebra (DLA) and rank of quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) for five HVAs within invariant subspaces; VQE experiments for ground state energy; analysis of loss function landscape and gradient descent convergence.
AI.result: Overparameterization coincides with the disappearance of local minima in the loss function; decay rate of VQE loss under gradient descent scales linearly with the number of ansatz parameters.
AI.conclusion: These results enrich the theory of quantum circuit overparameterization and guide the design of scalable variational ansatzes that respect symmetries.

title: Tight relation between the physical effects of a quantum measurement and the information gained about an observable
summary: The dynamics of quantum measurements defines a precise relation between the information gained about one physical property of a system and the observable changes in another physical property of the same system. Here, we express this relation in terms of the Hilbert space superpositions of the corresponding eigenstates and show how the probability of an observable physical change can be obtained from the Bayesian update of the probabilities associated with the information obtained in the measurement. Our analysis demonstrates that the superposition principle provides the tightest possible expression of the trade-off between information and back action in a quantum measurement.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the trade-off between information gain and back action in quantum measurements is fundamentally governed by the superposition principle, deriving it via Bayesian probability updates and Hilbert space superpositions.
AI.motivation: To express the relation between information gained about one physical property and observable changes in another property in quantum measurements, and to demonstrate that the superposition principle provides the tightest possible expression of the information-back action trade-off.
AI.method: The relation is expressed in terms of Hilbert space superpositions of corresponding eigenstates, and the probability of observable physical change is derived from Bayesian updates of probabilities associated with measurement information.
AI.result: The superposition principle provides the tightest possible expression of the trade-off between information and back action in a quantum measurement.
AI.conclusion: The dynamics of quantum measurements defines a precise relation between information gain and back action, with the superposition principle fundamentally constraining this trade-off.

title: Double-bracket quantum algorithms for thermal state preparation
summary: We propose quantum algorithms for preparing thermal states via the simulation of the thermofield double states. The key idea is to leverage double-bracket quantum algorithms to implement imaginary-time evolution on thermofield double states, whose reduced state realizes the Gibbs state. Our method, termed double-bracket thermofield double (DB-TFD), introduces two variants. The first, the vanilla DB-TFD algorithm, directly implements imaginary-time evolution using double-bracket quantum imaginary-time evolution. The second, poly DB-TFD, employs double-bracket quantum signal processing to approximate the imaginary-time evolution operator via a polynomial transformation. We demonstrate that the complexity of the poly DB-TFD algorithm scales exponentially with the inverse temperature in a broad practical regime. This scaling is consistent with existing methods, and numerical simulations support the corresponding theoretical bound. We further demonstrate the utility of DB-TFD in quantum Boltzmann machines for generative modeling, achieving improved performance compared with variational imaginary-time evolution approaches. These results establish DB-TFD as a promising route for thermal state preparation in the near-term and early-fault-tolerant regimes.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes double-bracket quantum algorithms (DB-TFD) for preparing thermal states by simulating thermofield double states via imaginary-time evolution. Two variants are introduced: vanilla DB-TFD (direct imaginary-time evolution) and poly DB-TFD (polynomial approximation using quantum signal processing). The latter scales exponentially with inverse temperature, matching existing methods, and shows improved performance in quantum Boltzmann machines over variational approaches.
AI.motivation: To develop efficient quantum algorithms for thermal state preparation, which is crucial for quantum statistical mechanics and quantum machine learning applications like Boltzmann machines.
AI.method: Two double-bracket thermofield double (DB-TFD) algorithms: (1) vanilla DB-TFD using double-bracket quantum imaginary-time evolution directly; (2) poly DB-TFD using double-bracket quantum signal processing to approximate imaginary-time evolution via a polynomial transformation.
AI.result: The poly DB-TFD algorithm's complexity scales exponentially with inverse temperature in a broad practical regime, consistent with existing methods. Numerical simulations validate the theoretical bound. DB-TFD outperforms variational imaginary-time evolution in quantum Boltzmann machine generative modeling.
AI.conclusion: DB-TFD algorithms offer a promising route for thermal state preparation suitable for near-term and early-fault-tolerant quantum devices.

title: Magnetic flux as a quantized Lorentz pseudoscalar and its relation to electric charge quantization
summary: In this paper, we re-examine the well-known question of why electric charges exist only in quantized portions. In this context, we revisit the motion of a charged particle in a field-free region around a current-carrying solenoid. Solving the corresponding Schrödinger equation leads to a simultaneous quantization condition for the magnetic flux and the electric charge. We also demonstrate the Lorentz invariance of this condition by showing that the magnetic flux behaves like a pseudoscalar under Lorentz transformations.

AI.tldr: This paper re-examines electric charge quantization by analyzing charged particle motion around a current-carrying solenoid, deriving a simultaneous quantization condition for magnetic flux and electric charge, and demonstrating its Lorentz invariance.
AI.motivation: To re-examine and provide a fresh perspective on the fundamental question of why electric charge exists only in discrete (quantized) portions.
AI.method: The authors revisit the motion of a charged particle in a field-free region around a current-carrying solenoid, solve the corresponding Schrödinger equation, and analyze the Lorentz transformation properties of the magnetic flux.
AI.result: A simultaneous quantization condition for magnetic flux and electric charge is derived. The magnetic flux is shown to behave as a pseudoscalar under Lorentz transformations, confirming the Lorentz invariance of the derived quantization condition.
AI.conclusion: The quantization of electric charge and magnetic flux are intrinsically linked and Lorentz invariant, offering a consistent theoretical framework for understanding charge quantization.

title: Efficient Quantum Circuit Construction of Controlled Time-Evolution for Arbitrary Pauli-Sum Hamiltonians
summary: Controlled time-evolution circuits select forward or backward Hamiltonian time evolution according to the state of an ancilla qubit. They are fundamental building blocks in quantum eigenvalue transformation of unitaries, Hamiltonian filtering, and related quantum algorithms. A direct realization adds ancilla control to the elementary gates of the time-evolution circuit and therefore increases the two-qubit gate count, compiled T depth and CX depth. We develop an efficient recursive algorithm that, for an arbitrary Pauli-sum Hamiltonian, partitions the input Pauli terms into groups and assigns to each group a sign-flip Pauli string that anti-commutes with the in-group terms, thereby removing ancilla control from the grouped time-evolution blocks. Numerical benchmarks on random Hamiltonians and structured spin Hamiltonians show reductions in compiled T depth and compiled CX depth. For a Kagome Hamiltonian with 24 spins under full connectivity, the proposed construction reduces the compiled T depth by 85.2% and the compiled CX depth by 68.9%, compared with a conventional implementation that decomposes the Hamiltonian into individual Pauli terms and implements the controlled time evolution of each term by directly adding the ancilla qubit to the corresponding Pauli-rotation circuit.

AI.tldr: A recursive algorithm partitions Pauli-sum Hamiltonian terms into groups with sign-flip strings to eliminate ancilla control from controlled time-evolution circuits, achieving up to 85.2% reduction in T depth and 68.9% reduction in CX depth on Kagome spin Hamiltonians.
AI.motivation: Controlled time-evolution circuits are essential for quantum eigenvalue transformation and Hamiltonian filtering, but direct ancilla control adds significant two-qubit gate overhead (increased T depth and CX depth). The goal is to reduce this overhead by eliminating ancilla control from grouped time-evolution blocks.
AI.method: A recursive algorithm that partitions Pauli terms into groups and assigns sign-flip Pauli strings anti-commuting with in-group terms, removing the need for ancilla control on grouped time-evolution blocks.
AI.result: Numerical benchmarks on random Hamiltonians and structured spin Hamiltonians show reductions in compiled T depth and CX depth. For a 24-spin Kagome Hamiltonian, compiled T depth reduced by 85.2% and CX depth by 68.9% compared to conventional term-by-term ancilla-controlled Pauli rotation implementations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed recursive grouping algorithm significantly reduces gate complexity of controlled time-evolution circuits for Pauli-sum Hamiltonians, improving the efficiency of quantum algorithms relying on these building blocks.

title: Deployed trusted-node quantum key distribution over 300 km with a multi-core fiber access link
summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is increasingly considered for deployment in realistic communication networks, where long distances, heterogeneous fiber infrastructure, and coexistence with classical traffic present substantial challenges. Here, we demonstrate trusted-node QKD between Linköping University and the Stockholm hub of the Swedish national quantum communication infrastructure over 270 km of deployed single-mode fiber, extended by a 33 km multi-core fiber (MCF) segment emulating a metropolitan access link, for a total distance of 303 km. The two sub-links use commercial QKD systems whose receivers are interfaced with external superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, enabling operation at losses beyond those supported by standard internal gated-mode detectors. We operate the link while actively switching the QKD channel between two MCF cores, with co-propagating Ethernet traffic and injected broadband optical noise in the other cores. The results demonstrate the integration of commercial QKD into demanding, dynamically reconfigurable fiber infrastructure relevant to future hybrid quantum-classical networks. Finally, using the generated secret keys, we illustrate how limited and time-varying QKD throughput affects one-time-pad-protected image transmission: image fidelity depends strongly on the available QKD-generated key budget and the choice of compression algorithm, highlighting application-level challenges for QKD-based encryption in realistic scenarios.

AI.tldr: A 303 km trusted-node QKD demonstration over deployed fiber (270 km SMF + 33 km MCF) in Sweden, using commercial QKD systems with external SNSPDs, active core switching, co-existing with classical traffic, and analyzing application-level impacts on one-time-pad image transmission.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate the feasibility of integrating commercial QKD systems into realistic, long-distance, heterogeneous fiber networks with coexisting classical traffic and dynamically reconfigurable infrastructure, bridging the gap between lab demonstrations and practical deployment.
AI.method: Trusted-node QKD over 270 km deployed SMF plus 33 km MCF segment using commercial QKD systems with external superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs); active switching of QKD channel between two MCF cores; co-propagation with Ethernet traffic and broadband optical noise. Application-level analysis using OTP-protected image transmission.
AI.result: Successful QKD operation over 303 km total distance with losses beyond standard gated-mode detector capabilities; demonstrated active core switching and coexistence with classical traffic; image transmission fidelity depends strongly on key budget and compression algorithm choice.
AI.conclusion: Commercial QKD can be integrated into demanding, reconfigurable fiber networks for future hybrid quantum-classical systems, but application-layer encryption must account for limited and time-varying key rates.

title: Multiple Quantum Hypothesis Testing: One-Shot Pairwise Bounds and Sharp Asymptotics
comment: arXiv:1401.7658, arXiv:1508.06624, arXiv:quant-ph/0607216. We are sorry if the accented character "ł" does not display properly through arXiv's TeX encoding of Metadata
summary:
We consider Bayesian discrimination among multiple quantum states and establish a dimension-free one-shot upper bound on the minimum probability of error in terms of the sum of pairwise errors. This resolves a conjecture of Audenaert and Mosonyi [J. Math. Phys. 55 (2014)] and improves the multiple quantum Chernoff bound of Li [Ann. Statist. 44 (2016)] by removing its dimension-dependent prefactor. In the asymptotic many-copy regime, our bound proves the achievability of the multiple quantum Chernoff distance for arbitrary separable Hilbert spaces, thereby settling the previously open infinite-dimensional case, and further yields constant-factor sharp asymptotics for the optimal error probability.
  In binary quantum hypothesis testing, we prove that the minimum error probability is characterized, up to universal constants, by a trace harmonic-mean quantity. Consequently, the optimal binary quantum error probability is within a factor of two of the optimal classical error probability for the associated Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions, complementing the lower bound of Nussbaum and Szkoła [Ann. Statist. 37 (2009)].

AI.tldr: This paper resolves a conjecture on Bayesian multiple quantum state discrimination, providing a dimension-free error bound, improving the multiple quantum Chernoff bound, settling the infinite-dimensional case, and proving that binary quantum error probability is characterized (up to constants) by a trace harmonic-mean quantity, with near-optimal classical-to-quantum gap.
AI.motivation: To resolve the conjecture of Audenaert and Mosonyi regarding dimension-free one-shot upper bounds for Bayesian multiple quantum state discrimination, and to settle the infinite-dimensional case of the multiple quantum Chernoff distance.
AI.method: The paper establishes a dimension-free one-shot upper bound on the minimum probability of error expressed as a sum of pairwise errors. For binary hypothesis testing, the error probability is characterized via a trace harmonic-mean quantity up to universal constants.
AI.result: The dimension-free bound improves Li's multiple quantum Chernoff bound by removing its dimension-dependent prefactor. In the asymptotic regime, achievability of the multiple quantum Chernoff distance is proven for arbitrary separable Hilbert spaces, yielding constant-factor sharp asymptotics. For binary testing, the optimal quantum error probability is within a factor of two of the optimal classical error probability for Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions.
AI.conclusion: The conjecture is resolved; the infinite-dimensional case is settled; and a tight classical-quantum error probability gap is established for binary discrimination.

title: Non-equilibrium thermodynamics of collapse models in the strongly non-Gaussian regime
summary: Standard objective collapse models offer a unified approach to the quantum measurement problem but predict an unphysical, indefinite increase in the energy of the system. The dissipative Diósi-Penrose (dDP) model resolves this heating issue by introducing a linear friction mechanism. However, this modification induces complex, non-Gaussian phase-space dynamics. We rigorously establish the thermodynamic consistency of this friction mechanism -- extended to the CSL model -- across both weakly and strongly non-Gaussian regimes. Using the Wigner phase-space formalism, we go significantly beyond the quadratic approximation and, to bypass the failure of perturbative methods under strong dissipation, introduce a novel exact pseudo-spectral simulation approach. Our analysis reveals that the system subjected to the dDP mechanism does not thermalize, but rather settles into a non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS) where the asymptotic non-Gaussianity scales as the third power of the dissipation parameter $β$. By evaluating the Wigner entropy production, we confirm the thermodynamic validity of the model and demonstrate that highly sensitive information-theoretic quantities require exact numerical methods to accurately capture the key non-Gaussian tails of the distribution.

AI.tldr: The dissipative Diósi-Penrose (dDP) model resolves the energy divergence issue in objective collapse models but introduces non-Gaussian dynamics. Using the Wigner formalism and a novel exact pseudo-spectral method, the authors prove the model's thermodynamic consistency. The system reaches a non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS) with non-Gaussianity scaling as β³, and exact numerics are essential to capture the non-Gaussian tails critical for information-theoretic quantities.
AI.motivation: Standard objective collapse models suffer from an unphysical indefinite energy increase (heating problem). The dissipative Diósi-Penrose (dDP) model introduces friction to address this, but its thermodynamic consistency had not been rigorously established beyond quadratic approximations, especially in strongly dissipative regimes where perturbative methods fail.
AI.method: The authors employ the Wigner phase-space formalism to go beyond the quadratic approximation. They develop a novel exact pseudo-spectral simulation approach to bypass the failure of perturbative methods under strong dissipation. The analysis is extended to the CSL model, and thermodynamic consistency is evaluated via Wigner entropy production.
AI.result: The system does not thermalize but reaches a non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS). The asymptotic non-Gaussianity scales as the third power of the dissipation parameter β. Exact numerical methods are required to accurately capture the key non-Gaussian tails of the distribution, which perturbative approaches miss.
AI.conclusion: The dDP friction mechanism (extended to CSL) is thermodynamically consistent across both weakly and strongly non-Gaussian regimes. Sensitive information-theoretic quantities depend on exact numerical treatment to properly resolve the non-Gaussian structure of the steady-state.

title: Quantum Algorithms for Triangle Cut Sparsification
summary:
Triangles capture higher-order structures in graphs and are fundamental to applications such as clustering and network analysis.
  To enable efficient use of such structures at scale, we study the problem of \emph{triangle cut sparsification}, which aims to reduce the graph size while approximately preserving triangle counts across every cut.
  We investigate \emph{quantum algorithms} for this problem, using triangle listing as our main technical ingredient.
  In particular, we present a quantum algorithm for triangle listing that, for a graph with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges, and $t$ triangles, runs in time $T_{\mathrm{q\text{-}list}} =$ $\widetilde{O}\bigl(\min(n^{5/4}t^{7/12} + n^{7/6}t^{7/9}, m + m^{3/4}t^{1/2},$ $n^{3/2}t^{1/2})\bigr)$, improving upon the best known classical bounds over a broad range of parameters. Our algorithm is based on a heavy-light vertex partition and an extension of triangle detection via quantum walks and Grover search.
  Leveraging this result, we design a quantum algorithm for constructing $\varepsilon$-triangle cut sparsifiers of size $\widetilde{O}(n/\varepsilon^2)$ in time $\widetilde{O}(T_{\mathrm{q\text{-}list}} + \sqrt{mn}/\varepsilon)$.
  Finally, we demonstrate applications to clustering algorithms based on triangle-related measures
  and prove a lower bound of $Ω(n/\varepsilon^2)$ on the size of any $\varepsilon$-triangle cut sparsifiers.

AI.tldr: This paper presents quantum algorithms for triangle cut sparsification, improving upon classical bounds with a quantum triangle listing algorithm running in $\widetilde{O}\bigl(\min(n^{5/4}t^{7/12} + n^{7/6}t^{7/9}, m + m^{3/4}t^{1/2}, n^{3/2}t^{1/2})\bigr)$ time, and constructs $\varepsilon$-triangle cut sparsifiers of size $\widetilde{O}(n/\varepsilon^2)$ in $\widetilde{O}(T_{\mathrm{q\text{-}list}} + \sqrt{mn}/\varepsilon)$ time, with a matching lower bound of $\Omega(n/\varepsilon^2)$.
AI.motivation: Triangles capture higher-order graph structures essential for clustering and network analysis, but processing them at scale is computationally demanding. The paper aims to reduce graph size while preserving triangle counts across cuts (triangle cut sparsification) and leverage quantum algorithms to achieve speedups over classical methods.
AI.method: The quantum triangle listing algorithm uses a heavy-light vertex partition combined with quantum walks and Grover search. This listing subroutine is then employed to construct $\varepsilon$-triangle cut sparsifiers via quantum sampling techniques.
AI.result: The quantum triangle listing algorithm achieves time $\widetilde{O}\bigl(\min(n^{5/4}t^{7/12} + n^{7/6}t^{7/9}, m + m^{3/4}t^{1/2}, n^{3/2}t^{1/2})\bigr)$, outperforming classical bounds over a broad parameter range. The resulting sparsifier has size $\widetilde{O}(n/\varepsilon^2)$ with construction time $\widetilde{O}(T_{\mathrm{q\text{-}list}} + \sqrt{mn}/\varepsilon)$, and a lower bound of $\Omega(n/\varepsilon^2)$ is proven.
AI.conclusion: Quantum algorithms can significantly accelerate triangle cut sparsification, with applications to clustering algorithms based on triangle-related measures. The size lower bound shows the construction is near-optimal.

title: Quantum enhanced rare event discovery and sampling
summary: Financial crashes, cascading failures in infrastructure, and critical errors in AI systems are frequently triggered by events that occur with extremely small probability. Efficiently discovering and sampling events with probability below a threshold is therefore of critical interest. Yet this task is highly non-trivial using existing classical or quantum methods. Being rare, such events require an immense sampling overhead to collect sufficient data samples. Moreover, because the rare events are not known in advance, they cannot be flagged for amplification using standard techniques. Here, we introduce a quantum algorithm for rare-event discovery and sampling without first learning which events are rare. The algorithm achieves the optimal quantum scaling with the rarity threshold. We further demonstrate that this can achieve a quadratic speedup for heavy-tailed systems whose tail has nonvanishing total mass, and translates into a robust polynomial speedup for stationary stochastic processes, with the exponent determined by its entropy-rate structure.

AI.tldr: A quantum algorithm for rare-event discovery and sampling achieves optimal quantum scaling and quadratic speedup for heavy-tailed systems and polynomial speedup for stationary stochastic processes, without needing prior knowledge of which events are rare.
AI.motivation: Financial crashes, infrastructure failures, and AI errors are triggered by extremely low-probability events. Efficiently discovering and sampling such rare events is critically important but highly challenging with classical or quantum methods due to immense sampling overhead and the inability to pre-identify events for amplification.
AI.method: The paper introduces a quantum algorithm for rare-event discovery and sampling that does not require first learning which events are rare. It achieves optimal quantum scaling with the rarity threshold.
AI.result: The algorithm achieves optimal quantum scaling with the rarity threshold, quadratic speedup for heavy-tailed systems with nonvanishing tail mass, and robust polynomial speedup for stationary stochastic processes with exponent determined by entropy-rate structure.
AI.conclusion: The proposed quantum algorithm provides provable speedups for rare-event sampling across different probabilistic regimes, addressing a fundamental challenge in stochastic systems.

title: Reliability of asymptotic work extraction
summary: Extracting work from quantum states is a fundamental task in quantum thermodynamics. Previous studies have primarily focused on determining the best achievable rate of work extraction, and remarkably, this characterization appeared to remain unchanged regardless of the choice of allowed processes: whether one considers the operationally motivated class of energy-conserving thermal operations, or the axiomatic class of Gibbs-preserving operations, the optimal extractable work is given by the Helmholtz free energy. Here, we challenge this perspective, showing that a more refined analysis of the asymptotic performance of work extraction reveals significant differences in the performance for the two different classes of free operations. Precisely, we focus on the trade-off between the extraction rate and its reliability, characterized by the optimal asymptotic speed at which the extraction error can be suppressed. We establish that the reliability of Gibbs-preserving operations and of thermal operations are respectively characterized by the Petz and the sandwiched Rényi relative entropies, demonstrating that the former in general strictly outperforms the latter, and providing new interpretations of several information-theoretic divergences. Our analysis reveals that operational constraints such as energy conservation impose stronger limitations on the achievable precision of quantum tasks than can be inferred from their asymptotic rates, thereby questioning the use of Gibbs-preserving operations as a mathematically convenient substitute for the physically realizable thermal processes.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that while both thermal operations and Gibbs-preserving operations yield the same optimal work extraction rate (Helmholtz free energy), they differ significantly in reliability (error suppression speed). Thermal operations are fundamentally limited by the sandwiched Rényi relative entropy, while Gibbs-preserving operations achieve the Petz Rényi relative entropy, meaning the latter is strictly more powerful. This challenges the common practice of substituting Gibbs-preserving operations for physically realizable thermal operations.
AI.motivation: To challenge the prevailing view that thermal operations and Gibbs-preserving operations are equivalent in work extraction, by analyzing the asymptotic trade-off between extraction rate and reliability (error suppression speed) rather than just the optimal rate.
AI.method: The authors analyze the asymptotic performance of work extraction under two classes of free operations—energy-conserving thermal operations and axiomatic Gibbs-preserving operations—by characterizing the optimal asymptotic speed at which extraction error can be suppressed, using Petz and sandwiched Rényi relative entropies as key information-theoretic tools.
AI.result: The reliability of Gibbs-preserving operations is characterized by the Petz Rényi relative entropy, while thermal operations are characterized by the sandwiched Rényi relative entropy; the former strictly outperforms the latter, revealing that operational constraints (energy conservation) impose stronger limitations on precision than on asymptotic rates.
AI.conclusion: Gibbs-preserving operations are not a physically faithful substitute for thermal operations when precision matters, undermining their use as a mathematically convenient proxy for realizable thermal processes in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Benchmarking Floquet Master Equations for Periodically Driven Open Quantum Systems
summary: The dynamics of open quantum systems is commonly described by quantum master equations derived under the assumption of weak system-bath coupling and a separation of timescales between system and bath. When the system is additionally subjected to a periodic driving, the validity of the resulting Floquet master equations is further restricted to regimes of weak or high-frequency driving. Here, we benchmark a set of commonly used Floquet master equations for a model of two locally driven spins coupled to a shared Ohmic reservoir at finite temperature. We systematically probe the accuracy of the equations as a function of the driving parameters, thus identifying limits of their applicability. Dynamical maps predicted by each master equation are compared against numerically exact non-Markovian simulations, tracking the full relaxation dynamics. We find that the accuracy of each master equation closely reflects the assumptions underlying its derivation. For the Floquet-Lindblad equation, errors can be strongly amplified near resonances where the secular approximation breaks down, while approaches that avoid the secular approximation perform better and exhibit a more systematic dependence of the error on driving frequency and amplitude.

AI.tldr: This paper benchmarks various Floquet master equations for open quantum systems under periodic driving, comparing their predictions to numerically exact non-Markovian simulations for two locally driven spins coupled to a shared Ohmic bath.
AI.motivation: To identify the limits of applicability of commonly used Floquet master equations and understand how their underlying assumptions affect accuracy, particularly for driven open quantum systems where standard weak-coupling master equations may break down.
AI.method: A set of Floquet master equations (including Floquet-Lindblad and secular-approximation-avoiding variants) are benchmarked against numerically exact non-Markovian simulations for a model of two locally driven spins coupled to a shared finite-temperature Ohmic reservoir, systematically probing driving parameter regimes.
AI.result: The accuracy of each master equation closely reflects its derivation assumptions. The Floquet-Lindblad equation shows strongly amplified errors near resonances due to secular approximation breakdown, while secular-approximation-avoiding approaches perform better with more systematic error dependence on driving frequency and amplitude.
AI.conclusion: Care must be taken when choosing Floquet master equations for driven open quantum systems; avoiding the secular approximation yields more reliable and systematically behaved dynamics across driving parameters.

title: A framework for low-overhead quantum fault tolerance via spacetime lifting
summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computation is inherently a spacetime problem, requiring not merely good static quantum error-correcting codes but also low-overhead protocols for protecting and manipulating encoded quantum information over time. Fault complexes provide a homological framework for treating such protocols as single spacetime objects. In this work, we initiate the study of low-overhead fault complexes by introducing {spacetime lifting}, a method that constructs fault complexes from symmetry-reduced product structures beyond standard foliation. We show that spacetime lifting yields fault complexes and in particular {spacetime-lifted} memory experiments with almost-linear fault distance in the total spacetime cost, which substantially outperforms existing constructions. We further interpret fault complexes as measurement-based cluster-state protocols and identify general conditions under which they realize fault-tolerant logical teleportation, showing that spacetime-lifted constructions combine favorable scaling with operational schemes. Our study opens a path toward more efficient quantum fault tolerance through general complex constructions.

AI.tldr: Introduces spacetime lifting, a method to construct fault complexes (spacetime objects for fault-tolerant quantum computation) from symmetry-reduced product structures, achieving almost-linear fault distance in total spacetime cost and enabling fault-tolerant logical teleportation via measurement-based cluster-state protocols.
AI.motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation is inherently a spacetime problem—requiring not just static quantum error-correcting codes but also low-overhead protocols for protecting and manipulating encoded quantum information over time. Fault complexes provide a homological framework for treating such protocols as single spacetime objects, and this work aims to improve their overhead and scaling.
AI.method: Proposes spacetime lifting, a method that constructs fault complexes from symmetry-reduced product structures beyond standard foliation. Interpretations of fault complexes as measurement-based cluster-state protocols are also used to derive general conditions for fault-tolerant logical teleportation.
AI.result: Spacetime lifting yields fault complexes with almost-linear fault distance in the total spacetime cost, substantially outperforming existing constructions. Spacetime-lifted constructions combine favorable scaling with operational schemes for fault-tolerant logical teleportation.
AI.conclusion: This work opens a path toward more efficient quantum fault tolerance through general complex constructions, demonstrating that spacetime lifting can significantly improve overhead scaling while maintaining operational viability.

title: Robustness of Entanglement Manipulation for almost i.i.d. sources
summary: We study the robustness of asymptotic entanglement manipulation beyond the exact i.i.d. regime, focusing on Mazzola--Sutter--Renner (MSR) almost i.i.d. sources, which allow a sublinear number of deviations from a tensor-power structure. For pure MSR sources along a bipartite reference state $|φ\rangle_{AB}$, we prove that the entanglement concentration rate is robust: every rate below the entropy of entanglement $S(φ_A)$ remains achievable. Moreover, this can be done by a single Schur--Weyl concentration protocol that is universal within the MSR class, depending only on the reference state and not on the particular source sequence. For mixed MSR sources along a reference state $ρ_{AB}$, we prove a source-dependent entanglement-distillation achievability result: every rate below the coherent information $I(A\rangle B)_ρ$ of the reference state is achievable, although the entanglement distillation protocol may depend on the particular MSR source sequence. For the reverse task of entanglement dilution, we prove a rate-robustness theorem: the asymptotic entanglement cost of any MSR target sequence along $ρ_{AB}$ is at most $E_F^\infty(ρ_{AB})$, the regularized entanglement of formation of the reference state. To establish these results, we prove structural and entropic properties of MSR almost i.i.d. sequences which may be useful in other information-theoretic settings. Thus, for the achievability statements considered here, MSR almost i.i.d. perturbations exhibit the same asymptotic behaviour as their i.i.d. reference states, despite allowing sublinear deviations from a tensor-power structure.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that asymptotic entanglement manipulation rates for pure and mixed almost i.i.d. (MSR) sources are robust: achievable rates match those of the i.i.d. reference state despite sublinear deviations, and key structural/entropic properties of MSR sequences are established.
AI.motivation: To understand whether entanglement manipulation rates remain robust beyond the exact i.i.d. regime, specifically under MSR almost i.i.d. sources that allow sublinear deviations from a tensor-power structure.
AI.method: The authors develop structural and entropic properties of MSR almost i.i.d. sequences, and apply Schur–Weyl concentration protocols (for pure states) and source-dependent distillation protocols (for mixed states) to establish achievability results.
AI.result: For pure MSR sources, every rate below the entropy of entanglement is achievable via a universal Schur–Weyl protocol. For mixed MSR sources, every rate below the coherent information is achievable with a source-dependent protocol. For entanglement dilution, the cost is bounded by the regularized entanglement of formation of the reference state.
AI.conclusion: MSR almost i.i.d. perturbations exhibit the same asymptotic behaviour as their i.i.d. reference states for the considered achievability tasks, despite allowing sublinear deviations from tensor-power structure.

title: Nanostructure modelling with early fault tolerant quantum computers
summary: Semiconductor nanostructures are central to many developing technologies. Notably, double quantum dots are especially important for semiconductor spin-qubit architectures, quantum sensing applications, and quantum-dot solar cells. Accurate modelling is highly desirable but conventional methods can struggle when dynamics involve more than two interacting electrons. In this work, we present a quantum simulation framework capable of addressing multi-electron double quantum dots. We adopt an efficiently scaling 1$^\text{st}$ quantised representation of the system and develop algorithms based on both Trotterisation and qubitisation. Incorporating insights from classical simulations enables us to produce resource estimates that are more realistic than those obtained from theoretical error bounds. Using a standard surface code model with physical noise at $10^{-3}$, our results indicate that the ground-state energy of four electrons in a double quantum dot can be estimated in approximately 24 hours using 226k physical qubits, or an eight-electron system in 3.4 days with 314k qubits (with runtimes falling dramatically when more qubits are available). We anticipate that incorporating very recent advances including dense surface code architectures (Low et al. arXiv:2605.30455) may reduce these costs significantly further. We conclude that early fault tolerant computers may prove to be valuable tools for designing mature-era quantum technologies.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a quantum simulation framework for multi-electron double quantum dots using first-quantised representation with Trotterisation and qubitisation algorithms, estimating ground-state energies of 4-electron (226k qubits, ~24 hrs) and 8-electron (314k qubits, ~3.4 days) systems under a surface code model with physical noise at 10^{-3}.
AI.motivation: Semiconductor nanostructures, especially double quantum dots, are crucial for spin-qubit architectures, quantum sensing, and quantum-dot solar cells. Accurate modelling of multi-electron dynamics is challenging for conventional methods, motivating the need for a quantum simulation framework.
AI.method: Adopts an efficiently scaling 1st quantised representation of the system and develops algorithms based on both Trotterisation and qubitisation. Classical simulation insights are incorporated to produce more realistic resource estimates than theoretical error bounds. A standard surface code model with physical noise at 10^{-3} is used.
AI.result: Ground-state energy of four electrons in a double quantum dot can be estimated in ~24 hours using 226k physical qubits; an eight-electron system in 3.4 days with 314k qubits. Runtimes decrease dramatically when more qubits are available.
AI.conclusion: Early fault tolerant quantum computers may prove valuable for designing mature-era quantum technologies. Recent advances like dense surface code architectures (Low et al.) could reduce costs further.

title: Energy-Modulated Time-Asymmetric Spontaneous Collapse: Forward-Backward Dynamics from Stochastic Ito Reversal and Bright Solitons
summary: We present a rigorous theoretical framework for symmetry breaking and quantum irreversibility arising from stochastic Ito field reversal within a cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrodinger equation (CQ-NLSE) formalism. Starting from three physically motivated considerations, forward and backward nonlinear stochastic differential equations are derived via the Ito calculus. Kinematic time-reversal is shown to be fundamentally incompatible with the Ito stochastic structure, yielding the universal asymmetry-coupling parameter of 2/3. An energy-driven collapse operator proportional to the product of noise strength, local probability density, and excitation energy squared is introduced, amplifying the collapse in high-density, high-excitation regions. Exactly bright soliton solutions are obtained for a quasi-one-dimensional BEC of attractive Li-7 atoms, with forward and backward amplitude ratio of 1.870. Heat map analysis of the parameter planes reveals that the forward collapse operator grows monotonically in time while the backward counterpart decays, achieving a ratio approximately 1030, sharply distinguishing this framework from conventional symmetric collapse models.

AI.tldr: A theoretical framework is developed for symmetry breaking and quantum irreversibility using stochastic Ito field reversal in cubic-quintic NLSE. The approach yields a universal asymmetry parameter of 2/3, an energy-driven collapse operator, bright soliton solutions for Li-7 BEC with forward/backward amplitude ratio 1.870, and a collapse operator ratio of ~10^30 distinguishing it from symmetric models.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous theoretical foundation for understanding symmetry breaking and quantum irreversibility by resolving the incompatibility between kinematic time-reversal and Ito stochastic calculus in nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics.
AI.method: Stochastic Ito calculus is applied to derive forward and backward nonlinear stochastic differential equations from three physical considerations. An energy-driven collapse operator proportional to noise strength, local probability density, and squared excitation energy is introduced. Analytical and numerical analysis of parameter planes is conducted.
AI.result: Universal asymmetry-coupling parameter of 2/3; exact bright soliton solutions for quasi-1D BEC of attractive Li-7 with forward/backward amplitude ratio 1.870; forward collapse operator grows monotonically while backward decays, achieving ratio ~10^30.
AI.conclusion: The framework sharply distinguishes itself from conventional symmetric collapse models, demonstrating fundamental irreversibility arising from the Ito stochastic structure in CQ-NLSE.

title: Breakeven demonstration of quantum low-density parity-check codes
summary: High-rate quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes are a leading candidate for fault-tolerant quantum computing. They feature higher encoding rates than planar alternatives such as the surface code, but their implementation often entails significant hardware hurdles like the need for long-range couplers. We leverage the flexibility of a trapped-ion quantum computer to demonstrate nine quantum error-correcting codes with starkly different qubit connectivity requirements on a single device without any hardware reconfiguration. These experiments span three families of quantum error-correcting codes: qLDPC codes, topological codes, and concatenated codes. With a qLDPC code encoding 4 logical qubits into 18 physical qubits, we achieve a logical error rate up to $9\times$ better than a previous demonstration of a similar code on superconducting solid-state qubits. Moreover, our implementation exhibits breakeven performance, with some instances achieving qubit lifetimes comparable to or slightly exceeding that of our trapped-ion qubits. We use a novel implementation of the optical-metastable-ground (OMG) architecture for addressable mid-circuit measurement and reset, which enables us to perform these experiments without any ion transport or dedicated coolant ions, requirements that typically consume a large fraction of the runtime or ion count of trapped-ion quantum computers.

AI.tldr: Researchers used a trapped-ion quantum computer with a novel OMG architecture to demonstrate nine quantum error-correcting codes—including qLDPC, topological, and concatenated codes—without hardware reconfiguration, achieving a qLDPC logical error rate up to 9× better than prior superconducting qubit demonstrations and breakeven performance in qubit lifetime.
AI.motivation: High-rate qLDPC codes offer better encoding rates than planar codes like the surface code but require challenging long-range couplers in hardware. The authors aim to demonstrate that trapped-ion platforms, with their flexible connectivity, can implement diverse QEC codes without hardware reconfiguration, overcoming this hurdle.
AI.method: Experiments are conducted on a trapped-ion quantum computer using a novel optical-metastable-ground (OMG) architecture for addressable mid-circuit measurement and reset, eliminating the need for ion transport or dedicated coolant ions. Nine QEC codes from three families (qLDPC, topological, concatenated) are implemented on the same device with no hardware reconfiguration.
AI.result: A qLDPC code encoding 4 logical qubits into 18 physical qubits achieved logical error rates up to 9× better than a previous superconducting qubit demonstration. Some instances achieved breakeven performance with qubit lifetimes comparable to or slightly exceeding that of the trapped-ion qubits.
AI.conclusion: Trapped-ion platforms are highly versatile for implementing diverse quantum error-correcting codes, and the OMG architecture efficiently supports mid-circuit measurement and reset without costly ion transport or coolant ions, paving the way for more practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantum element-wise transforms
summary: Quantum algorithms for basic numerical linear algebraic tasks have proven essential for translating diverse problems to a unified quantum computational context. Many of these tasks -- e.g., applying a polynomial function to the spectrum of a matrix embedded in a unitary process (a so-called block encoding), or taking linear combinations of block encodings -- are well-addressed by techniques like quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) or linear combination of unitaries (LCU). However, there exist useful matrix transforms whose realization by existing quantum algorithms is unclear or inefficient. In this work we construct improved quantum algorithms for some of these transforms, the simplest of which is a polynomial function applied element-wise. We show the space required to compute quantum element-wise transforms can be reduced exponentially in the degree of the applied function compared to prior work, and raise and rectify errors in previous constructions. We present our algorithms alongside applications to machine learning, simulation, and signal processing.

AI.tldr: This work constructs improved quantum algorithms for element-wise polynomial transforms on matrices, reducing space requirements exponentially in the polynomial degree compared to prior work, and correcting errors in previous constructions. Applications to machine learning, simulation, and signal processing are presented.
AI.motivation: Many useful matrix transforms (e.g., element-wise polynomial functions) lack clear or efficient realization by existing quantum algorithms like QSVT or LCU, motivating the need for improved quantum methods for these transforms.
AI.method: The authors construct improved quantum algorithms for element-wise polynomial transforms, achieving exponential reduction in space complexity relative to the degree of the applied function. They also identify and rectify errors in prior constructions.
AI.result: Space required for computing quantum element-wise transforms can be reduced exponentially in the degree of the applied function compared to prior work.
AI.conclusion: The proposed algorithms provide efficient quantum solutions for element-wise matrix transforms, with demonstrated applications in machine learning, simulation, and signal processing.

title: Nonreversible Gauge Fields in Fokker--Planck Dynamics: Supersymmetric Hamiltonians and Learned Finite Forces
summary: We formulate stationary-density-preserving nonreversible perturbations of Fokker--Planck dynamics as gauge fields that deform relaxation spectra while leaving the invariant state fixed. When detailed balance holds, a similarity transformation maps the reversible Fokker--Planck operator to a Witten-Laplacian-type supersymmetric Hamiltonian; nonreversible gauges then appear as non-Hermitian perturbations that preserve the zero mode but modify the excited spectrum. This operator viewpoint gives a common language for relaxation gaps, circulating probability currents, hypocoercive acceleration, and finite control costs. We represent admissible gauge currents by antisymmetric tensor fields and identify the detailed-balance-violating Ohzeki--Ichiki force as a constant symplectic example whose infinite-strength limit is Hamiltonian dynamics. The continuous-time spectral gap alone does not select a finite gauge strength, so we introduce a finite-time regularized objective and an actor--critic procedure for learning the gauge. An exactly solvable anisotropic Gaussian Ornstein--Uhlenbeck benchmark separates the spectral transition from the finite-time optimum and shows that the learned gauge recovers the Lyapunov-equation optimum. A double-well benchmark then illustrates the same constrained selection in a nonconvex metastable landscape. Stochastic gradient methods enter this framework as physically relevant Fokker--Planck systems: mini-batch noise acts as an effective diffusion tensor, and adaptive methods such as Adam correspond to metric choices with possible nonequilibrium currents.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates nonreversible perturbations of Fokker-Planck dynamics as gauge fields that preserve the stationary distribution but modify relaxation spectra, connecting this framework to hypocoercive acceleration, control costs, and stochastic optimization methods like Adam.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified operator-theoretic language for understanding how nonreversible perturbations accelerate convergence to equilibrium while preserving the invariant state, and to connect this to optimal control and machine learning optimization methods.
AI.method: Formulates nonreversible perturbations as antisymmetric tensor (gauge) fields applied to Fokker-Planck operators; uses similarity transformations to map reversible dynamics to supersymmetric Hamiltonians; introduces a finite-time regularized objective with an actor-critic learning procedure to select optimal gauge strength.
AI.result: Exactly solvable anisotropic Gaussian Ornstein-Uhlenbeck benchmark shows separation between spectral transition and finite-time optimum; learned gauge recovers the Lyapunov-equation optimum. Double-well benchmark demonstrates constrained selection in metastable landscapes. Connects mini-batch noise to effective diffusion and Adam to metric choices with nonequilibrium currents.
AI.conclusion: The gauge-field perspective unifies relaxation gaps, circulating currents, hypocoercive acceleration, and control costs, and provides a principled way to design nonreversible dynamics for accelerated sampling and optimization.
